title: Windy Weather
whatItIs: Strong winds can push vehicles and riders off course, especially in gusts and on exposed roads.
keyFacts: High-sided vehicles are most affected, but gusts can also push cars, cyclists, motorcyclists and horse riders.
Expect sudden gusts on exposed open roads, when passing bridges and at gaps in hedges.
Give cyclists, motorcyclists and horse riders extra room: they may be blown into your path.
Keep well back from motorcyclists overtaking a high-sided vehicle in strong wind.

items.title: Open roads
items.text: Exposed stretches with nothing to block a crosswind.

items.title: Bridges
items.text: Passing bridges can expose you to strong gusts.

items.title: Gaps in hedges
items.text: Passing a gap in a hedge can let a strong gust hit you.

items.title: Passing large vehicles
items.text: The air around them can push smaller vehicles and riders.

a.label: Passing a lorry in wind
points: Turbulence can push you off course

b.label: Passing a cyclist in wind
points: They may wobble or be blown out

onTheTest.question: It is very windy. You are about to overtake a cyclist. What should you do?
options: Sound your horn as you pass
onTheTest.why: A gust can push a cyclist into your path, so leave extra room when you overtake.

traps: Gaps in hedges and passing bridges can bring sudden strong gusts.
Wind affects cars too, not just lorries and vans.
Motorcyclists overtaking a lorry can be hit by turbulence: keep well back.

sources.ref: Rules 163 and 212 (Extra space in high winds)
